clue.text: A check on stock in a minor way

definitions.text: A check on stock in a minor way

parts.words: A check on stock in a minor way
parts.note: a barrier of spaced bars set into a country lane stops livestock straying while letting vehicles pass

explanation.surface: Sounds like a small audit of a shop's inventory, done modestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' suggests goods on a shelf and 'minor way' a small degree, but the stock is farm animals and the minor way is a country road.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid of metal bars across a rural road lets cars cross while hooves cannot, so it is a check on livestock.

clue.text: Without entitlement right away

explanation.surface: Lacking any right, and at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon abbreviates anonymous, without a name or title; it also archaically means immediately or soon.

clue.text: Whisper, but not very much

explanation.surface: A murmur of very little substance.
explanation.definitionFit: To tittle is a dialect verb for gossiping in whispers; a tittle is also a tiny amount, a jot.

clue.text: Erotic love leaving painter absorbed — quite irregular!

indicators.note: absorbed means the painter is taken into what is left
leaving signals that the letter for love departs from the word Erotic

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
RA, Royal Academician, denotes a painter

explanation.surface: Passion fading while an artist is engrossed in work, most unpredictable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes O from EROTIC, giving ERTIC; 'absorbed' puts RA inside to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means unpredictable or inconsistent in behaviour or pattern.

clue.text: Regret shown about a large number being vulgar

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: to rue is to regret
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Someone shows sorrow over many being coarse.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude can mean crude or indecent, as of a joke.

clue.text: Wearing apparel

parts.note: the phrase reads as a noun for clothing but also describes someone who has clothes on

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing apparel' looks like the old phrase for clothing; read as a description, it means having clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with clothes on is clothed, attired or garbed.

clue.text: Allowed fool to back up heel, an artist

indicators.note: in a down clue back up means the preceding words are read in reverse, from bottom to top

parts.note: let means allowed
a sap is a fool
a ship heels or lists when it leans over

explanation.surface: A permitted idiot propping up a scoundrel, who turns out to be a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back up' turns the run LETSAP into PASTEL. 'heel' looks like a cad but is the nautical verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastellist is one who draws or paints with pastel crayons.

clue.text: Town in southern England that's broken the records

indicators.note: broken means the letters of the record words are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A town that has beaten all the records.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorchester is the county town of Dorset, in south-west England. 'broken the records' sounds like setting new bests.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorchester is the county town of Dorset on England's south coast region.

clue.text: Turncoat censor

indicators.note: the front half of the word Turncoat tells us to turn the rest of it about, rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: A traitorous official who vets what may be published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turncoat' reads as one word for a traitor; split it, and 'Turn' rearranges COAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Porcius Cato held the Roman office of censor and is remembered by that title.

clue.text: A walkover!

parts.note: a walkover usually means an easy win, but read literally it is something you walk over

explanation.surface: An exclamation at an easy victory.
explanation.walkthrough: The sporting sense of an effortless win is the decoy; the literal sense is a structure pedestrians cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow bridge for people on foot is literally something one walks over.

clue.text: Corrupt after a month in charge

parts.note: Sept is the short form of September

explanation.surface: Someone turns crooked after only a month holding the reins.
explanation.definitionFit: A septic wound is infected and putrid, which is to say rotten or tainted.

clue.text: "Sea-fire" — odd name for a flower

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters of the quoted word are in a strange order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange coinage, sea-fire, presented as the name of a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The freesia is a fragrant South African plant grown for its funnel-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Considered people dumping leader to be base

parts.note: found as in 'found him guilty' means judged or considered

indicators.note: dumping leader means the first letter of the people word is dropped

parts.note: a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Judged a nation that ousts its leader to be contemptible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like an adjective meaning low, but it is the noun for a foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundation is the bottom support on which a building rests.

clue.text: Oriental girl negotiating a rise for agents

parts.note: E stands for east, the Orient
a miss is a girl

indicators.note: negotiating suggests working the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An Eastern woman bargaining for a pay increase on behalf of representatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Emissaries are envoys or representatives sent on a mission.

clue.text: Some double-dealer, thoroughly wide-awake

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A thoroughly watchful cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert means being fully attentive, awake to everything.

clue.text: Note beans are repellent

definitions.note: here a noun: something that drives back

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
pulses are edible seeds such as beans and lentils

explanation.surface: A remark that beans are disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repellent' looks like an adjective for the beans, but it defines a rebuff that drives something back.
explanation.definitionFit: A repulse is a rebuff or driving back, the act of repelling.

clue.text: Odd scholar organizing a dance

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate scholar

explanation.surface: A peculiar academic putting on a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Many commend this guy

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
to laud is to praise or commend

explanation.surface: Plenty of people speak well of a certain fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Claud is a man's first name, so it can stand for some fellow.

clue.text: One's written an article in French on electronic communication

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
IT, information technology, covers computing and electronic communication

explanation.surface: Someone has penned a French-language piece about email.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places UN before IT in a down-style charade; 'One's written' hides the definition One.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing, the number one in counting.

clue.text: Tomb of channel islands holy man

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, off the coast of Normandy
St is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: The burial place of a saint from Jersey or Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: A cist is a prehistoric stone burial chamber, a box-like grave.

clue.text: Public relations order that's sound

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire, an honour

explanation.surface: A publicity department's instruction that is judged reasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable, but it is a verb meaning to investigate.
explanation.definitionFit: To sound a depth or a person is to probe, testing or exploring them.

clue.text: Argue in favour of trial

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: Make a case in support of a test case.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest is to object or declare forcefully, to make one's case.

clue.text: Middle-of-the-road issue about one's eating

indicators.note: Middle-of picks the central three letters of the road words
about means the issue word goes round the letter for one

parts.note: a son is offspring, issue
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A moderate matter concerning someone's diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle-of-the-road' reads as moderate; instead take the middle three letters of THEROAD. 'eating' looks like dining but means wearing away.
explanation.definitionFit: Erosion is a gradual wearing away, as water corrodes rock.

clue.text: Go off accepting second course

indicators.note: accepting means the first word takes the second into itself

parts.note: to desert is to leave or go off

explanation.surface: Leaving the table just as the next part of the meal arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet is served as the last course of a meal.

clue.text: Judge taking part in rare settlement

indicators.note: settlement is read as the letters being settled into a new order

parts.note: a bit is a part or piece

explanation.surface: A magistrate involved in an unusual agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' joins BIT to RARE; the letters of RAREBIT are then rearranged by 'settlement'.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter decides disputes, acting as referee or umpire.

clue.text: Raise new money in this country

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of Raise form a fresh word

parts.note: L is the symbol for the pound, money

explanation.surface: Fund-raising in a particular nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a nation in the Middle East.

clue.text: The economy calls for a little growth

explanation.surface: Thrift policy demands a modest rise in output.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrift is careful saving, economy with money; it is also sea pink, a small tufted plant.

clue.text: An economist's works

explanation.surface: A reference to what an economist produced.
explanation.definitionFit: John Stuart Mill was a Victorian economist and philosopher; a mill is also a factory, a works.

clue.text: Looks up and down

indicators.note: in a down clue up and down means the word reads the same in either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Glances up and down at something.
explanation.definitionFit: To see is to look at or observe.

clue.text: In time lead could well be done away with

indicators.note: could well be suggests the letters may take another form, a cue to rearrange them

explanation.surface: Given time, a leading position may disappear.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliminated means removed or got rid of entirely.

clue.text: Frank wants nothing put down on paper

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
to pen is to write

explanation.surface: A man called Frank wants nothing written down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' seems to be a person's name; it is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being frank is being candid and plain-spoken.

clue.text: Reserve troops made smaller advance, lacking ability

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was the British army's volunteer reserve
to advance money is to lend it, so advance gives lent
less means smaller in amount

explanation.surface: Reservists made a smaller push forward because they were incompetent.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA was the British Territorial Army, its part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Without talent means having no skill or gift.
